chapter: Chicago and New York with Louis Armstrong, 1925-30
title: Clarence Jones's band at the Metropolitan Theater with Louis
summary: With Jimmy Noone at the Nest, Zutty joined pianist Clarence Jones at the Metropolitan Theater, a movie house where he and Louis did an act and he wore a dress for a comic number.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Then he says, with Jimmy Noone at Nest before joining the Clarence Jones band at the Metropolitan Theater with Louis Armstrong.
That's right.
Well who was Clarence Jones, a piano player?
Yes, yes he was a good piano player.
He wrote a lot of numbers.
He wrote a lot of fine tunes.
And he wanted Fats Waller (unintelligible) and Fats Waller (unintelligible). And Clarence Jones' name is on one of the numbers.
Was he related to that Richard, was he related to Richard M. Jones?
No. No, no relation at all. Richard he was from New Orleans. He was from New Orleans.
Well this band at the Metropolitan Theater that was playing a show?
No. It was just, Louis and I would put on an act every now and then.
Oh yes?
You know we'd get up on the stage.
That was a picture house wasn't it?
Yes.
A movie house. And the band would play rag time.
We did a tune once that if I can't play first fiddle I aint going to play no fiddle at all. And I'd have on a dress and everything.
Just you and Louis?
Me and Louis, yes Louis and I.
Sort of an intermission like. They'd put the lights on and they'd do the show. And the band would play too.
And Jimmy Bell was our leader at one time. And Carroll Dickerson was a leader there also.
That was, that was, wasn't that the job where you replaced Jimmy Bertrand at?
No.
Who was with him before?
Some other drummer.
Gee, I can't remember.
Yes, and then there was another drummer and they gave you the job.
They gave me the job because Clarence Jones hired a leader and a drummer. I followed somebody in that but I can't remember.
It wasn't Bertrand then?
No it wasn't Bertrand. Because Bertrand he played at the (Van Dorn?).
That's right.
Well how long roughly would that have lasted at the Metropolitan?
It must have lasted about a year or more.
